items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ

transliteration.en: Bismillāh, tawakkaltu ʿalā Allāh, wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh

translation.en: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah.

text.en: Whoever says, when he leaves his house, “In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah,” it is said to him: you are guided, sufficed and protected.
text.ar: مَنْ قَالَ — يَعْنِي إِذَا خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ — بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَلاَ حَوْلَ وَلاَ قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ

why.en: A sentence at the door that hands the day over to Allah before it starts. The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever says it is guided, provided for and protected as they go out.

reminder.en: Said at the door, before the day takes over. It is short enough to become the thing you do without thinking about it.

how.en: Pause at the door as you leave.
Say the words once, quietly or aloud.
Step out.

transliteration.en: Allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik

translation.en: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

text.en: When one of you enters the masjid, let him say: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

why.en: The masjid is a place of mercy, so you ask for mercy as you walk in. It also marks the change from the street to the prayer.

reminder.en: A word of asking as you step through, before you look for a place in the row.

how.en: Step in with your right foot.
Say the dua as you enter.

items.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ

transliteration.en: Subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn

translation.en: Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, when we could never have done it ourselves; and to our Lord we shall surely return.

text.en: When the Prophet mounted his camel to set out on a journey he would say: Glory be to the One who has subjected this to us, when we could never have done it ourselves.

why.en: The travel dua thanks Allah for the means of travel and asks for an easy road and a safe return. It is said once the journey is actually under way.

reminder.en: Said once you are settled and moving, at the start of the road rather than in the rush of leaving.

how.en: Once seated and moving, say Allahu Akbar three times.
Say the dua.
Ask for ease, safety and a good return in your own words if you like.

transliteration.en: Bismika-llāhumma amūtu wa aḥyā

translation.en: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

text.en: When the Prophet went to bed he would say: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

why.en: The last words of the day, given to Allah. Saying them makes sleep itself an act of remembrance.

reminder.en: The last words of the day, after the phone is down. It takes less time than lying there deciding to sleep.

how.en: Lie down on your right side if you can.
Say the words once.

items.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ

transliteration.en: Al-ḥamdu lillāhi-lladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhi-n-nushūr

translation.en: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.

text.en: When the Prophet woke he would say: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.

why.en: Waking is a small return to life, and the first words of the day thank the One who gave it back.

reminder.en: The first words of the day, before anything else asks for your attention.

how.en: Say the words as soon as you are awake, before anything else.

transliteration.en: Bismillāh

translation.en: In the name of Allah.

text.en: The Prophet said to a boy in his care: Say the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you.

why.en: Naming Allah over food is the difference between eating and eating with gratitude. If you forget and remember mid-meal, there is a form for that too.

reminder.en: Before the first bite. A pause of two seconds that turns a meal into something noticed.

how.en: Say Bismillah before the first bite.
If you forget, say: Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirahu (in the name of Allah at its beginning and its end).

transliteration.en: Subḥāna-llāh

translation.en: Glory be to Allah.

text.en: Whoever glorifies Allah thirty-three times after each prayer, praises Him thirty-three times and magnifies Him thirty-three times, then completes the hundred, his sins are forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.

why.en: Thirty-three each of Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu Akbar after every prayer, completed with one phrase to make a hundred. The Prophet ﷺ said sins are forgiven for it, however many.

reminder.en: Said sitting, before you stand and the moment has gone. Thirty-three, thirty-three, thirty-four.

how.en: After the prayer, say Subhan Allah 33 times.
Say Alhamdulillah 33 times.
Say Allahu Akbar 33 times.
Complete the hundred with: La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa ala kulli shay'in qadir.

text.en: Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.
Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing stands between him and entering Paradise but death.

why.en: One verse, recited after each prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said nothing stands between the one who recites it after prayer and entering Paradise except death.

reminder.en: Recited once you have finished, while you are still sitting where you prayed.

how.en: After the tasbih, recite Ayat al-Kursi (Qur'an 2:255) once.

text.en: Were it not that it would burden my ummah, I would have ordered them to use the siwak at every prayer.

why.en: Cleaning the teeth before standing to pray. A toothbrush serves the same purpose where there is no siwak.

reminder.en: Cleaning the teeth before standing to pray. A toothbrush does the same work where there is no siwak.

how.en: Before the prayer, clean the teeth with a siwak or a brush.

text.en: The two rak’ah before Fajr are better than the world and everything in it.

why.en: Two short rak'ah before the Fajr prayer. Of all the voluntary prayers, this is the one the Prophet ﷺ never left, even when travelling.

reminder.en: Two short rak’ah once Fajr has entered, before the fard. The Prophet ﷺ kept to these more closely than any other voluntary prayer.

how.en: After the Fajr adhan and before the obligatory prayer, pray two rak'ah.
Keep them short.
Then pray Fajr.

text.en: Whoever prays twelve rak’ah in a day and a night, a house will be built for him in Paradise.

why.en: Two rak'ah after the Dhuhr prayer, part of the twelve daily rawatib for which the Prophet ﷺ promised a house in Paradise.

reminder.en: Prayed after the fard, while you are still standing where you prayed.

how.en: After the Dhuhr prayer and its dhikr, pray two rak'ah.

text.en: When one of you has prayed the Jumu'ah, let him pray four after it.
He would not pray after the Jumu'ah until he had left, and then he would pray two rak'ah.

note.en: Four rak'ah are narrated for after Jumu'ah, and two prayed at home. Scholars reconcile the two differently.

why.en: The voluntary prayer after Jumu'ah, which on a Friday takes the place of the two rak'ah after Dhuhr. The Prophet ﷺ told those who pray Jumu'ah to pray four after it, and he himself prayed two once he had left for home.

reminder.en: Prayed after Jumu'ah: four in the masjid, or two once you are home.

how.en: After Jumu'ah and its dhikr, pray four rak'ah in the masjid, as two pairs.
Or pray two rak'ah once you are home.

text.en: The best manner of seeking forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant.

why.en: A set of remembrances said between Fajr and sunrise, or in the morning generally. They frame the day before it fills with everything else.

reminder.en: The morning remembrance, kept between Fajr and sunrise. The Prophet ﷺ would sit in remembrance after the morning prayer until the sun had risen.

how.en: After Fajr, sit a moment.
Say the morning adhkar, whose texts are below: Ayat al-Kursi, the three Quls, the sayyid al-istighfar, and the rest.
If you know only one or two, say those.

parts.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ

transliteration.en: Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwal-ḥayyul-qayyūm, lā taʾkhudhuhū sinatun wa lā nawm, lahū mā fis-samāwāti wa mā fil-arḍ, man dhal-ladhī yashfaʿu ʿindahū illā bi-idhnih, yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wa mā khalfahum, wa lā yuḥīṭūna bi-shayʾim-min ʿilmihī illā bimā shāʾ, wasiʿa kursiyyuhus-samāwāti wal-arḍ, wa lā yaʾūduhū ḥifẓuhumā, wa huwal-ʿaliyyul-ʿaẓīm.

translation.en: Allah: there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation does not tire Him. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

text.en: Allah: there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence.

parts.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhir-raḥmānir-raḥīm. Qul huwallāhu aḥad. Allāhuṣ-ṣamad. Lam yalid wa lam yūlad. Wa lam yakul-lahū kufuwan aḥad.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.

text.en: Say: He is Allah, the One.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.

parts.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ
مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ
وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhir-raḥmānir-raḥīm. Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabbil-falaq. Min sharri mā khalaq. Wa min sharri ghāsiqin idhā waqab. Wa min sharrin-naffāthāti fil-ʿuqad. Wa min sharri ḥāsidin idhā ḥasad.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.

text.en: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.

parts.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ
مَلِكِ النَّاسِ
إِلَهِ النَّاسِ
مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ
الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ
مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhir-raḥmānir-raḥīm. Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabbin-nās. Malikin-nās. Ilāhin-nās. Min sharril-waswāsil-khannās. Alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūrin-nās. Minal-jinnati wan-nās.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer, who whispers in the hearts of mankind, from among the jinn and mankind.

text.en: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.

parts.arabic: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ

transliteration.en: Aṣbaḥnā wa aṣbaḥal-mulku lillāh, wal-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr. Rabbi asʾaluka khayra mā fī hādhal-yawmi wa khayra mā baʿdah, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā fī hādhal-yawmi wa sharri mā baʿdah. Rabbi aʿūdhu bika minal-kasali wa sūʾil-kibar. Rabbi aʿūdhu bika min ʿadhābin fin-nāri wa ʿadhābin fil-qabr.

translation.en: We have reached the morning, and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no deity but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.

text.en: When evening came, the Prophet ﷺ would say: “We have reached the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah…” And in the morning he said the same: “We have reached the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah.”

title.en: By You we reach the morning

parts.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ

transliteration.en: Allāhumma bika aṣbaḥnā, wa bika amsaynā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilaykan-nushūr.

translation.en: O Allah, by You we reach the morning and by You we reach the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.

text.en: The Prophet ﷺ would teach his companions to say in the morning: “O Allah, by You we reach the morning and by You we reach the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection,” and in the evening: “O Allah, by You we reach the evening and by You we reach the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the return.”

parts.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ

transliteration.en: Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa ana ʿabduk, wa ana ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika mastaṭaʿt, aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt, abūʾu laka bi-niʿmatika ʿalayya, wa abūʾu laka bi-dhanbī faghfir lī, fa-innahū lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant.

translation.en: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep to Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.

text.en: The best manner of seeking forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant.

parts.arabic: رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ نَبِيًّا

transliteration.en: Raḍītu billāhi rabban, wa bil-islāmi dīnan, wa bi-Muḥammadin ﷺ nabiyyā.

translation.en: I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet.

text.en: Whoever says, in the morning and the evening, that he is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet, it is a right upon Allah to please him.

title.en: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing harms
title.ar: بسم الله الذي لا يضر مع اسمه شيء

parts.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhil-ladhī lā yaḍurru maʿasmihī shayʾun fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samāʾ, wa huwas-samīʿul-ʿalīm.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

text.en: Whoever says three times, “In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,” will not be struck by sudden affliction until morning, and whoever says it three times in the morning will not be struck by sudden affliction until evening.

No servant says, in the morning of every day and the evening of every night, “In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,” three times, and is then harmed by anything.

title.en: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him

parts.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ

transliteration.en: Subḥānallāhi wa bi-ḥamdih.

translation.en: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him.

text.en: Whoever says, in the morning and in the evening, “Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him” a hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better, except one who said the same or more.
The best manner of seeking forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant.

why.en: The evening counterpart, said between Asr and Maghrib or in the evening generally. The same protection and gratitude for the night as for the day.

reminder.en: The evening remembrance, from Asr until the light goes.

how.en: After Asr, sit a moment.
Say the evening adhkar, whose texts are below.
If you know only one or two, say those.

parts.arabic: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ

transliteration.en: Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwal-ḥayyul-qayyūm, lā taʾkhudhuhū sinatun wa lā nawm, lahū mā fis-samāwāti wa mā fil-arḍ, man dhal-ladhī yashfaʿu ʿindahū illā bi-idhnih, yaʿlamu mā bayna aydīhim wa mā khalfahum, wa lā yuḥīṭūna bi-shayʾim-min ʿilmihī illā bimā shāʾ, wasiʿa kursiyyuhus-samāwāti wal-arḍ, wa lā yaʾūduhū ḥifẓuhumā, wa huwal-ʿaliyyul-ʿaẓīm.

translation.en: Allah: there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation does not tire Him. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

text.en: Allah: there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence.

parts.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhir-raḥmānir-raḥīm. Qul huwallāhu aḥad. Allāhuṣ-ṣamad. Lam yalid wa lam yūlad. Wa lam yakul-lahū kufuwan aḥad.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.

text.en: Say: He is Allah, the One.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.

parts.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ
مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ
وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhir-raḥmānir-raḥīm. Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabbil-falaq. Min sharri mā khalaq. Wa min sharri ghāsiqin idhā waqab. Wa min sharrin-naffāthāti fil-ʿuqad. Wa min sharri ḥāsidin idhā ḥasad.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of those who blow on knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.

text.en: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.

parts.arabic:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ
مَلِكِ النَّاسِ
إِلَهِ النَّاسِ
مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ
الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ
مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhir-raḥmānir-raḥīm. Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabbin-nās. Malikin-nās. Ilāhin-nās. Min sharril-waswāsil-khannās. Alladhī yuwaswisu fī ṣudūrin-nās. Minal-jinnati wan-nās.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer, who whispers in the hearts of mankind, from among the jinn and mankind.

text.en: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.
Say “Qul huwa Allahu ahad” and the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and an-Nas, three times in the evening and in the morning; they will suffice you against everything.

parts.arabic: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكَسَلِ وَسُوءِ الْكِبَرِ، رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ

transliteration.en: Amsaynā wa amsal-mulku lillāh, wal-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr. Rabbi asʾaluka khayra mā fī hādhihil-laylati wa khayra mā baʿdahā, wa aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā fī hādhihil-laylati wa sharri mā baʿdahā. Rabbi aʿūdhu bika minal-kasali wa sūʾil-kibar. Rabbi aʿūdhu bika min ʿadhābin fin-nāri wa ʿadhābin fil-qabr.

translation.en: We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. There is no deity but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.

text.en: When evening came, the Prophet ﷺ would say: “We have reached the evening and the dominion belongs to Allah…” And in the morning he said the same: “We have reached the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah.”

title.en: By You we reach the evening

parts.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ

transliteration.en: Allāhumma bika amsaynā, wa bika aṣbaḥnā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilaykal-maṣīr.

translation.en: O Allah, by You we reach the evening and by You we reach the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the return.

text.en: The Prophet ﷺ would teach his companions to say in the morning: “O Allah, by You we reach the morning and by You we reach the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection,” and in the evening: “O Allah, by You we reach the evening and by You we reach the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the return.”

parts.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ

transliteration.en: Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa ana ʿabduk, wa ana ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika mastaṭaʿt, aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt, abūʾu laka bi-niʿmatika ʿalayya, wa abūʾu laka bi-dhanbī faghfir lī, fa-innahū lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant.

translation.en: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep to Your covenant and Your promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.

text.en: The best manner of seeking forgiveness is to say: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity but You. You created me and I am Your servant.

parts.arabic: رَضِيتُ بِاللَّهِ رَبًّا، وَبِالْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا، وَبِمُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ نَبِيًّا

transliteration.en: Raḍītu billāhi rabban, wa bil-islāmi dīnan, wa bi-Muḥammadin ﷺ nabiyyā.

translation.en: I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet.

text.en: Whoever says, in the morning and the evening, that he is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion and with Muhammad ﷺ as Prophet, it is a right upon Allah to please him.

title.en: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing harms
title.ar: بسم الله الذي لا يضر مع اسمه شيء

parts.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ

transliteration.en: Bismillāhil-ladhī lā yaḍurru maʿasmihī shayʾun fil-arḍi wa lā fis-samāʾ, wa huwas-samīʿul-ʿalīm.

translation.en: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

text.en: Whoever says three times, “In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,” will not be struck by sudden affliction until morning, and whoever says it three times in the morning will not be struck by sudden affliction until evening.

No servant says, in the morning of every day and the evening of every night, “In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,” three times, and is then harmed by anything.

title.en: Refuge in the perfect words of Allah

parts.arabic: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ

transliteration.en: Aʿūdhu bi-kalimātillāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.

translation.en: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.

text.en: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said he had been stung by a scorpion the night before. He said: “Had you said, when evening came, ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,’ it would not have harmed you.”

title.en: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him

parts.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ

transliteration.en: Subḥānallāhi wa bi-ḥamdih.

translation.en: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him.

text.en: Whoever says, in the morning and in the evening, “Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him” a hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better, except one who said the same or more.
The Prophet was asked about fasting on Monday and said: that is the day I was born, and the day I was sent, or the day revelation came to me.

why.en: The Prophet ﷺ fasted Mondays and Thursdays and said deeds are presented on those days. Monday is also the day he was born.

reminder.en: Monday was one of the two days the Prophet ﷺ returned to, week after week, through the year.

how.en: Decide the night before to fast.
Eat before Fajr if you can.
Fast from Fajr to Maghrib.

text.en: Deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday, and I like my deeds to be presented while I am fasting.

why.en: Thursday is the other weekly fast the Prophet ﷺ kept. One day a week is a manageable habit; two is his own.

reminder.en: Thursday, with Monday, was a fast he ﷺ kept regularly rather than occasionally.

how.en: Decide the night before to fast.
Eat before Fajr if you can.
Fast from Fajr to Maghrib.

text.en: My friend advised me to do three things: to fast three days of every month, to pray two rak’ah of Duha, and to pray Witr before sleeping.

note.en: The hadith establishes fasting three days of each month. Scholars differ on whether these must be the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth specifically.

why.en: Three days a month, on the 13th, 14th and 15th when the moon is full. The Prophet ﷺ compared fasting three days each month to fasting the whole year.

reminder.en: The thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth, when the moon is full. Three days a month, spaced so they never pile up.

how.en: Watch for the middle of the Islamic month; this app shows it a few days ahead.
Fast the 13th, 14th and 15th, or any three days of the month.

text.en: The Prophet found the Jews fasting on the day of Ashura, and said: we have more right to Musa than you — so he fasted it and ordered that it be fasted.

why.en: The 10th of Muharram. The Prophet ﷺ said fasting it expiates the sins of the year before, and recommended adding the 9th.

reminder.en: The tenth of Muharram. It is one day, and it is easier decided tonight than at dawn.

how.en: Fast the 10th of Muharram.
Add the 9th if you can.

title.en: Fasting on the day of Arafah

text.en: Fasting the day of Arafah expiates the sins of the preceding year and the coming year.

note.en: Scholars differ on whether this follows the local ninth of Dhul Hijjah or the day of standing at Arafah in Makkah when the two fall differently.

why.en: The 9th of Dhul Hijjah, the day the pilgrims stand at Arafah. For those not on Hajj, fasting it expiates two years of sins.

reminder.en: The ninth of Dhul Hijjah, for those who are not standing at Arafah.

how.en: Fast the 9th of Dhul Hijjah.
Not for pilgrims; they do not fast that day.

text.en: Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as though he fasted the whole year.

why.en: Six days of fasting in the month after Ramadan. With Ramadan they add up to what the Prophet ﷺ called fasting the whole year.

reminder.en: Six days, any six, anywhere in the month. They do not need to be kept together.

how.en: Any six days of Shawwal, together or apart, after the day of Eid.

text.en: My friend advised me to do three things: to fast three days of every month, to pray two rak’ah of Duha, and to pray Witr before sleeping.

why.en: A short voluntary prayer in the mid-morning. The Prophet ﷺ said the charity owed by every joint of the body is discharged by two rak'ah of Duha.

reminder.en: Prayed once the sun is well up and before Dhuhr. Two rak’ah are enough for it to count.

how.en: When the sun is well up and before midday, pray two rak'ah or more.

text.en: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer.

note.en: Scholars differ on whether shortening on a journey is obligatory or a concession that may be taken or left.

why.en: On a journey the four-rak'ah prayers are shortened to two. It is a gift, not a compromise, and the Prophet ﷺ always took it.

reminder.en: While you are travelling, the four-rak’ah prayers may be prayed as two.

how.en: While travelling, pray Dhuhr, Asr and Isha as two rak'ah each.
Fajr and Maghrib stay as they are.

title.en: Two or four rak’ah before Dhuhr

text.en: I memorised ten rak'ah from the Prophet ﷺ: two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib in his house, two after Isha in his house, and two before the Fajr prayer.

why.en: Two or four rak'ah before the Dhuhr prayer, the largest part of the daily rawatib. They settle you before the obligatory prayer rather than rushing into it.

reminder.en: Prayed after Dhuhr has entered and before the fard.

how.en: After the Dhuhr adhan and before the obligatory prayer, pray two rak'ah, or four as two pairs.
Then pray Dhuhr.

text.en: I memorised ten rak'ah from the Prophet ﷺ: two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib in his house, two after Isha in his house, and two before the Fajr prayer.

why.en: Two rak'ah after the Maghrib prayer. The Prophet ﷺ prayed them at home, which is where most people are at that hour anyway.

reminder.en: Two rak’ah after the fard, before the evening moves on to something else.

how.en: After the Maghrib prayer and its dhikr, pray two rak'ah.

text.en: I memorised ten rak'ah from the Prophet ﷺ: two before Dhuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib in his house, two after Isha in his house, and two before the Fajr prayer.

why.en: Two rak'ah after the Isha prayer, the last of the rawatib, usually prayed at home before Witr.

reminder.en: Two rak’ah after the fard, while you are still there.

how.en: After the Isha prayer and its dhikr, pray two rak'ah.

text.en: Make Witr the last of your prayer at night.

why.en: An odd number of rak'ah, often one or three, as the last prayer of the night. The Prophet ﷺ never left it, at home or on a journey, and told us to make it the last thing we pray.

reminder.en: The last prayer of the night, an odd number of rak’ah. If you are not sure of waking, it can be prayed before you sleep.

how.en: Any time after Isha and before Fajr, pray one rak'ah, or three.
If you fear you will not wake, pray it before sleeping.
Make it the last prayer of your night.

transliteration.en: Bismillāh

translation.en: In the name of Allah.

text.en: When a man enters his house and mentions Allah on entering and on eating, Shaytan says to his companions: you have no lodging here and no supper.

why.en: Mentioning Allah as you come in, and greeting whoever is there, keeps the home a place He is remembered in. The Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan finds no place to stay in such a house.

reminder.en: Said as you come through the door, before the house takes over.

how.en: Say Bismillah as you step in.
Greet those inside with as-salamu alaykum, even if the house is empty.

transliteration.en: Allāhu akbar

translation.en: Allah is the greatest.

text.en: When we went up we said Allahu Akbar, and when we came down we said Subhan Allah.

why.en: Allahu Akbar as you climb: a hill, a staircase, a lift. The companions did it on every rise of the road, and it turns an ordinary climb into remembrance.

reminder.en: Said going up — a staircase, a hill, a lift. A small word for a small climb.

how.en: As you start going up, say Allahu Akbar.

transliteration.en: Subḥāna-llāh

translation.en: Glory be to Allah.

text.en: When we went up we said Allahu Akbar, and when we came down we said Subhan Allah.

why.en: Subhan Allah as you descend, the pair to the takbir on the way up.

reminder.en: Said going down, as the takbir is said going up.

how.en: As you start going down, say Subhan Allah.

items.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ

transliteration.en: Bismillāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn, wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn

translation.en: In the name of Allah, praise be to Allah. Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have accomplished it by ourselves; and to our Lord we shall surely return.

text.en: Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have accomplished it by ourselves; and to our Lord we shall surely return.
When the Prophet ﷺ mounted his camel to set out on a journey, he would say Allahu Akbar three times, then: Glory to Him who has subjected this to us...

why.en: The words the Prophet ﷺ said on mounting his camel, which fit a car, a bus or a train exactly as well: this was put at our service, and we could not have done it ourselves.

reminder.en: Said once you are seated and the vehicle is moving.

how.en: Once seated, say Bismillah.
Say Alhamdulillah.
Say the verse: Subhan alladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun.

title.en: Before sleep: Ayat al-Kursi and the Quls

text.en: Every night when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed he cupped his hands, blew into them, recited Qul huwa Allahu ahad, Qul a'udhu bi Rabbi al-falaq and Qul a'udhu bi Rabbi an-nas, then wiped whatever he could of his body, beginning with his head and face and the front of his body, three times.
When you go to your bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi; a guardian from Allah will stay with you and no devil will approach you until morning.

why.en: A short set the Prophet ﷺ recited every night: Ayat al-Kursi, and the three short surahs beginning with Qul, blown into the hands and wiped over the body. He said a guardian stays with the one who recites Ayat al-Kursi until morning.

reminder.en: Ayat al-Kursi and the three Quls, last thing. About a minute, and the day is closed.

how.en: Recite Ayat al-Kursi (Qur'an 2:255).
Cup your hands, blow into them, and recite al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas.
Wipe your hands over as much of your body as you can reach, starting with the head and face.
Do the hands three times.

text.en: Whoever stands in prayer in Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins are forgiven.

why.en: The night prayer of Ramadan, prayed in congregation as Taraweeh or alone at home. The Prophet ﷺ promised forgiveness of past sins to whoever stands in it out of faith.

reminder.en: The night prayer in Ramadan, in the masjid or at home — however many rak’ah you can keep to.

how.en: After Isha, pray Taraweeh at the masjid or some rak'ah at home.
Any amount counts; keep what you can keep every night.

title.en: The first ten days of Dhul Hijjah

text.en: There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days.

why.en: The ten days leading to Eid al-Adha, which the Prophet ﷺ said hold deeds more beloved to Allah than on any other days. Fasting, dhikr and charity all count; the 9th is Arafah.

reminder.en: The first ten days of Dhul Hijjah. Ordinary good deeds are especially weighty in them.

how.en: Say Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu Akbar, wa lillahi al-hamd through the days.
Fast whichever of the first nine days you can.
Give something in charity.

text.en: When one of you comes to the Jumu'ah, let him perform ghusl.
Ghusl on Friday is obligatory upon everyone who has reached puberty, and that he use the siwak and apply perfume if he has some.

note.en: Most scholars hold the ghusl for Jumu'ah a strongly recommended sunnah. Some hold it obligatory, reading the word “obligatory” (wajib) in the hadith literally.

why.en: A full bath before going to Jumu'ah, with the siwak and perfume if you have some. The Prophet ﷺ told whoever comes to Jumu'ah to bathe for it, and named the siwak and perfume alongside it.

reminder.en: Before Jumu'ah: a ghusl, the siwak, and perfume if you have some.

how.en: Before setting out for Jumu'ah, wash the whole body.
Clean your teeth with a siwak or a brush.
Put on perfume if you have some.

text.en: Whoever performs ghusl on Friday like the ghusl for janabah and then goes to the prayer, it is as if he had offered a camel; whoever goes in the second hour, as if he had offered a cow; in the third hour, a horned ram; in the fourth hour, a hen; in the fifth hour, an egg. When the imam comes out, the angels come in to listen to the reminder.

why.en: Setting out for Jumu'ah well before the imam comes out. The Prophet ﷺ likened whoever goes in the first hour to someone offering a camel, and each later hour to a smaller offering, down to an egg. When the imam comes out, the angels come in to listen.

reminder.en: Going early to Jumu'ah: the earliest hour is likened to offering a camel.

how.en: After your ghusl, set out for the masjid early, well before the imam comes out.
Wait in the masjid until the imam comes out for the sermon.

text.en: Whoever reads Surat al-Kahf on Friday, light will shine for him between the two Fridays.

note.en: Since the Islamic day begins at Maghrib, scholars commonly hold that its time runs from Maghrib on Thursday until Maghrib on Friday. This app shows it for that span.

why.en: Al-Kahf, the eighteenth surah of the Quran, read once on Friday. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever reads it on Friday has light shining for him between that Friday and the next.

reminder.en: Friday begins at Maghrib tonight. Surah al-Kahf, read before the next Maghrib, brings light between the two Fridays.

how.en: Open Surah al-Kahf, the 18th surah, in a mushaf or a Quran app.
Read it in one sitting, or in parts across the day.
Its time runs from Maghrib on Thursday until Maghrib on Friday.

title.en: Abundant salawat on the Prophet ﷺ
title.ar: الإكثار من الصلاة على النبي ﷺ

text.en: Among the best of your days is Friday … so send abundant blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me.

why.en: Sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ many times through Friday. He named Friday among the best of days and told his followers to send abundant blessings on him in it, for their blessings are presented to him.

reminder.en: Tomorrow is Friday. Send abundant blessings on the Prophet ﷺ through it; they are presented to him.

how.en: Send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ in any words you know, such as the salah on him recited in the tashahhud.
Say it any number of times; the more, the better.
Return to it through the day.

title.en: Du’a in the last hour of Friday
title.ar: الدعاء في آخر ساعة من يوم الجمعة

text.en: In it there is an hour: no Muslim servant happens upon it while standing in prayer, asking Allah for something, except that He gives it to him.
…so seek it in the last hour after Asr.

note.en: Scholars name several times for this hour. The last hour after Asr is among the strongest views; some hold it is while the imam sits, until the prayer ends.

why.en: Friday holds an hour in which du'a is answered. The Prophet ﷺ said that no Muslim meets it, asking Allah for something, without being given it, and said to seek it in the last hour after Asr.

reminder.en: The last hour of Friday is here. Ask Allah for what you need before Maghrib.

how.en: Between Asr and Maghrib on Friday, set some time aside.
Ask Allah for what you need, for yourself and for others.
Keep asking until Maghrib if you can.
